text:
Anika: heads up — saw a ~4x jump in 95p latency on shared-gpu-pool-3 around 12:03 UTC, affects small-request tenants. Anyone on call?
deploy-bot: alert: pool=shared-gpu-pool-3 metric=serve_latency_95p value=420ms threshold=200ms window=5m link=https://ops.internal/alerts/2468100000 :rotating_light:
Jesse: seeing it too. quick peek at runtime logs — lots of kernel_autoswitch events right before the spike. suspecting kernel thrash with small batch traffic.
Charlie: can you paste the kernel-switch snippets + any batch-size distribution?
Jesse: here's a short extract from the profiler around 12:02:40-12:03:05:
```
profile snippet:
12:02:41 tenant=acme-svc kernel=fp16_optimized -> fp16_generic (autoswitch)
batch_sizes: 1,1,1,2,1,1,1,1,3,1
kv_cache_hits: 0.032 -> 0.009
kernel_switch_count(pool=3): 37 -> 112 (3s)
latency_95p(pool=3): 120ms -> 420ms
```
Jesse: small batch-heavy tenants appear to be toggling kernels frequently which triggers KV-cache thrash and eviction cascades.
Maya: confirmed — eviction rate for kv slots on pool-3 jumped x5, TTL-based warmups weren't keeping slots resident. Cold cache + kernel switch = slow token generation.
Anika: so the noisy neighbor is likely a handful of small-req tenants sending many 1-token/short requests causing the scheduler to flip kernels to cheaper path then back, losing KV locality.
Charlie: short-term mitigation idea: disable kernel_autoswitch for tenants with avg_batch_size < 2 for a short window (30-60s) and prefer stable kernel; that should reduce flip-rate and keep KV hot.
Maya: agree. also consider soft per-tenant kernel-switch rate limit metric (e.g., max 1 switch/30s) and a fallback policy to pin kernel if switch_count spikes.
Charlie: deploying a canary patch to pool-3 nodes now — command: 
```
opsctl config set pool=shared-gpu-pool-3 kernel_autoswitch.policy="pin_small_batch_kernel:true;batch_threshold:2;pin_window:60s"
opsctl rollout start pool=shared-gpu-pool-3 --canary=2
```
deploy-bot: started rollout canary -> nodes: gpu3-12,gpu3-15. status: in_progress
Jesse: canary result after 2m: 95p on canary nodes dropped from 420ms -> 110ms, kernel_switch_count down 85%. Overall pool 95p trending down.
Anika: nice. rolling to rest of pool. please add temporary grafana panels for per-tenant kernel_switch_count and kv_eviction_rate.
Charlie: created INF-1249 to track permanent fix: "per-tenant kernel-switch telemetry + alerting" and linked dashboard.
Maya: longer term notes: batching heuristic should be workload-aware; bursty tiny requests should either be batched more aggressively client-side or served on a kernel path that favors KV stability vs micro-ops perf. Also revisit KV slot sizing for tiny sequences.
Anika: quick follow-ups: 1) monitor kv_hitrate and kernel_switch_count for 1 hour post-rollout 2) evaluate adding a tiny-req tenant QoS (soft caps) 3) update runbook with this mitigation.
Jesse: added a short alert: alert if per-tenant kernel_switch_count > 10 within 60s.
Maya: postmortem TODO: quantify cost impact of pinning vs autoswitch savings, and update Optimize recommendations for customers that generate many tiny requests.
Anika: thanks team — closing this thread once metrics stable. :thumbsup:
